review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked the simp-tagged lemmas against each other and against the DFA, EpsilonNFA and Language files. The lemmas I checked were stepSet_*, evalFrom_*, eval_*, nil/cons/append_mem_acceptsFrom, acceptsFrom_union/iUnion, toNFA_evalFrom_match, toNFA_correct, toDFA_correct, reverse_reverse, mem_accepts_reverse and Path.supp.

Candidates I rejected:
- evalFrom_singleton and eval_singleton are rfl lemmas that evalFrom_cons plus evalFrom_nil already imply. DFA.lean (evalFrom_singleton, eval_singleton) and EpsilonNFA.lean (evalFrom_singleton, eval_singleton) have the same lemmas, and both sides rewrite to the same result, so this is harmless redundancy and not a defect.
- acceptsFrom_union has `+` on its right-hand side. Language.lean defines `+` on languages as union (`add_def`) and has simp lemmas stated with `+` (e.g. `reverse_add`, `add_self`), so `+` is the intended normal form.
- evalFrom_eq_biUnion_singleton, mem_stepSet and mem_evalFrom_iff_exists are not simp. That is sensible, because making evalFrom_eq_biUnion_singleton simp could cycle with singleton-set rewrites.
- cons_mem_acceptsFrom and append_mem_acceptsFrom overlap only on `a :: x ++ y`, which List.cons_append normalises first (my reasoning, not run).

I could not run Lean, so I did not check the simp-normal-form lint.
